title: Posted Schedule: The Monthly Carry Rate by the Condition the Grain Came In At
content:
The monthly carry rate on bushels standing unpriced under Grain Marketing Contracts rises with the condition the grain came in at, because grain taken in wet or damp costs the elevator more to hold.

| The parcel and the loads standing against the contract | Monthly carry rate |
|---|---|
| The parcel carries at least 1500 bushels and at least one load standing against the contract, whatever the disposition, was probed above the moisture base | 0.055 per bushel per month |
| At least one load was probed above the moisture base but the parcel falls short of 1500 bushels | 0.048 per bushel per month |
| No load was probed above the moisture base | the monthly rate the member's marketing programme carries |

## Which loads are read for the condition

Every load standing against the contract is read, whatever the disposition: a load the member directed to the contract at the scale and a load the member ran straight through to the buyer are both read, and one such load probed above the moisture base is enough.

## Both sides of the parcel size

The conditioned rate asks for two things together: a parcel of at least 1500 bushels, the figure itself qualifying, and at least one conditioned load standing against the contract. A parcel of 1500 bushels with one wet load takes 0.055. A parcel of 1499 bushels with the same wet load takes 0.048. A parcel of 40,000 bushels with no conditioned load at all takes neither figure, and is carried at the rate its marketing programme carries.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

A hypothetical parcel of 2,000 net bushels stands against a contract carrying one load probed damp. The rate is 0.055 per bushel per month, so three chargeable months on that parcel come to 330.00 before any other figure is brought to it. Had the parcel been 1,200 bushels, the rate would be 0.048, and three chargeable months would come to 172.80.
